Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

office noun

a public office

also public office, hold office, run for office, magistracy

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.5.35: quōs adhūc mihi magistrātūs populus Rōmānus mandāvit
Cic. Leg. 3.47: magistrātū abīre (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 353

magistrātus, magistrātūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a public office, a magistracy

magistrātum gerere, to hold office (Traupman 179); petere, to stand for it (Traupman 180); magistrātū abīre, to leave it. Also the official himself (see government).

Examples

  • ita quaestor sum factus ut mihi illum honōrem tum nōn sōlum datum, sed etiam crēditum et commissum putārem

    when I was made quaestor, I felt that the office had not only been given to me but entrusted and committed to my careCic. Verr. 2.5.35

  • populō, quī stultus honōrēs saepe dat indignīs

    the people, which is foolish enough often to give office to the unworthyHor. S. 1.6.15–16

  • Quōs honōrēs gessistī?

    What offices have you held?Traupman 175

Other words

  • honōs (honor), honōris m. — an office, a post of honour

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.35: ut mihi illum honōrem tum nōn sōlum datum, sed etiam crēditum et commissum putārem; Hor. S. 1.6.15–16; Traupman 175, 353

    The office as an honour the people confers; in the plural the offices of a public career. Cicero writes honōs, later authors honor (Lewis & Short).

See also position, government, political, office.

SourcesLewis & Short: magistratus · Lewis & Short: honor
